why: The notions agree. On the quadrant model, B's unit vectors lim (φ(z_k) − φ(z))/|φ(z_k) − φ(z)| (sequences z_k ∈ K∖{z} → z in M) are exactly the project's unitDirections of the chart image φ(V∩K) at φ(z) (glue lemma unitVecsB_eq: tails lie in the chart domain, where φ is injective and continuous, and φ⁻¹ is continuous on the target). Their span is the span of Mathlib's tangent cone (span_unitDirections, non-item), which is the project's relTangent: B (a), and B (c) for essentialSet. A ⇒ B: B (b) is A's span_tangentConeAt_chartImage_eq_map for e and chartAt z, after replacing fderivWithin on the chart-change domain by fderivWithin on range I. B ⇒ A fails on generality. A's chart-independence conjuncts hold for every model with corners (any normed E) and every C^k atlas with k ≠ 0; essentialSet_eq and the crossLines witnesses (model 𝓘(ℝ, Fin 2 → ℝ)) are not in B at all. On quadrant models with the C^∞ atlas, B does give A's first two conjuncts (chartIndep_of_B, relTangent_eq_map_of_B, via a chain rule for chart changes proved here), so the gap is A's extra generality and extra true content.
